atoms.b: All trees can be divided into the categories of evergreen and deciduous. ((++Evergreen Deciduous)) trees keep their leaves all year round. Deciduous trees lose their leaves in ((++winter summer)).
The leaves of deciduous trees also change colour. For example, in Autumn, deciduous trees’ leaves turn a shade of ((++orange pink)). Evergreen trees’ leaves remain green.
In the United Kingdom, there are only 5 native evergreen trees, but 50 different types of ((++deciduous decade)) trees.
Some common evergreen trees are spruce and ((++pine oak)). Some common deciduous trees are beech and ((++ash spruce)).

instruction.text: Are the following statements true or false?

atoms.a: Evergreen trees are more populous than deciduous trees in the UK.
The leaves on deciduous trees fall off at some point during the year.
The colour of deciduous trees’ leaves never changes.
An example of an evergreen tree is the pine tree.
An example of a deciduous tree is the beech tree.
